title: The Gathering
summary: King Mosiah gathers the people, assembled in two bodies: the people of Nephi and the people of Zarahemla.

explicit_facts.text: King Mosiah caused all the people to be gathered together.
The people of Nephi and the people of Zarahemla assembled together in two bodies.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Two distinct gathered crowds can be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact gathering place, clothing, architecture, and crowd size are not stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the historical arrival of Mulek's people as a present event.

title: The Peoples’ Relative Numbers
summary: The verses compare the numbers of the descendants of Nephi, the people of Zarahemla, and the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: The children and descendants of Nephi were fewer than the people of Zarahemla.
Zarahemla was a descendant of Mulek.
The people of Nephi and the people of Zarahemla together were less than half as numerous as the Lamanites.

unspecified_visual_details: No present visual moment or particular location is specified.

narration.text: And there were not so many of the people of Nephi and of the people of Zarahemla as there were of the Lamanites; yea, they were not half so numerous.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state relative population sizes rather than narrating an event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the groups gathered together or assign specific population counts.

title: Mosiah Reads Zeniff’s Records
summary: Mosiah reads the records of Zeniff to the people, covering the account from the people’s departure from Zarahemla until their return.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah read, and caused to be read, the records of Zeniff to his people.
The records covered the time from leaving Zarahemla until returning.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown reading to the gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: The records’ physical appearance and the setting are not specified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The records’ earlier events are reported, not depicted here as present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the departure, afflictions, or return as a flashback scene.

title: Mosiah Reads Alma’s Account
summary: Mosiah reads the account of Alma and his brethren and their afflictions, from their departure from Zarahemla until their return.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah read the account of Alma and his brethren and their afflictions.
The account covered the time from leaving Zarahemla until returning.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown reading to the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, records’ appearance, and listeners’ individual reactions are not specified here.

title: Wonder and Joy
summary: Mosiah finishes reading the records. His people who tarried in the land are struck with wonder and amazement, then behold those delivered out of bondage and are filled with exceedingly great joy.
characters: His people who tarried in the land

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah made an end of reading the records.
His people who tarried in the land were struck with wonder and amazement.
When they beheld those delivered out of bondage, they were filled with exceedingly great joy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Those delivered out of bondage may be visible to the people who behold them.
unspecified_visual_details: The verses do not specify the setting, the people's appearance, or their gestures.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the delivered people by names or group labels not given in these verses.
Do not depict the earlier bondage or deliverance as occurring now.

title: Sorrow for the Slain
summary: Thinking of their brethren slain by the Lamanites, the people grieve and shed tears.

explicit_facts.text: The people thought of their brethren who had been slain by the Lamanites.
They were filled with sorrow and shed many tears.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The gathered people may be shown weeping.
unspecified_visual_details: The slain brethren are not shown; their identities and the place of their deaths are unstated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the killings as a present event.

title: Thanks to God
summary: Remembering God’s goodness and power in delivering Alma and his brethren, the people raise their voices and give thanks to God.

explicit_facts.text: The people thought of God’s goodness and power in delivering Alma and his brethren from the Lamanites and bondage.
They raised their voices and gave thanks to God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown raising their voices together.
unspecified_visual_details: The passage gives no exact words of thanks or visible depiction of God.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent spoken words or portray God as visibly present.

title: Anguish for the Lamanites
summary: Thinking of the Lamanites as their brethren and of their sinful and polluted state, the people feel pain and anguish for their souls.

explicit_facts.text: The people thought upon the Lamanites, whom they considered their brethren, and their sinful and polluted state.
They felt pain and anguish for the welfare of the Lamanites’ souls.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown in sorrowful reflection.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lamanites are the subject of the people’s thoughts, not necessarily present.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The description of the Lamanites’ state is the people’s reported thought.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lamanites as present or invent visible spiritual conditions.

title: The Children Choose a Name
summary: The children of Amulon and his brethren, displeased with their fathers’ conduct, refuse their fathers’ names and take the name of Nephi to be numbered among the Nephites.
characters: Children of Amulon and his brethren

explicit_facts.text: The children of Amulon and his brethren were displeased with their fathers’ conduct and would no longer be called by their fathers’ names.
They took upon themselves the name of Nephi to be called the children of Nephi and numbered among the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The children may be shown together as a group.
unspecified_visual_details: Their ages, individual identities, location, and any formal naming ceremony are not stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a ceremony, individual names, or visible actions beyond the stated change of name.

title: Zarahemla Numbered with the Nephites
summary: All the people of Zarahemla were numbered with the Nephites because the kingdom had been conferred only on descendants of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: All the people of Zarahemla were numbered with the Nephites.
The kingdom had been conferred on none but descendants of Nephi.

unspecified_visual_details: No specific present action or visible people are described.

narration.text: And now all the people of Zarahemla were numbered with the Nephites, and this because the kingdom had been conferred upon none but those who were descendants of Nephi.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a ceremony or portray the conferral of the kingdom as a new event.

title: Alma Teaches the Assemblies
summary: Alma preaches repentance and faith on the Lord as he goes from one large body of assembled people to another. He exhorts Limhi’s people and those delivered from bondage to remember the Lord’s deliverance.

explicit_facts.text: Alma spoke to the people assembled in large bodies, going from one body to another and preaching repentance and faith on the Lord.
Alma exhorted Limhi’s people and all those delivered from bondage to remember that the Lord delivered them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be depicted addressing one gathered body at a time.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact words of the preaching and the location are not supplied.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Teaching is summarized in the source; do not turn its summary into invented dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent exact sermon wording.

title: The Desire for Baptism
summary: After Alma finishes teaching, King Limhi and all his people desire baptism.

explicit_facts.text: After Alma taught many things and finished speaking, King Limhi desired baptism.
All Limhi’s people also desired baptism.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi and his people may be shown expressing their desire to be baptized.
unspecified_visual_details: No request in the form of dialogue is given; the place and gestures are unspecified.

title: Alma Baptizes Limhi’s People
summary: Alma goes into the water and baptizes those who believe his words; those baptized belong to the church of God.

explicit_facts.text: Alma went forth into the water and baptized them after the manner he baptized his brethren in the waters of Mormon.
Those he baptized belonged to the church of God because of their belief on Alma’s words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A baptism in water may be depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: The water’s location, baptismal method, and number of people baptized are not specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the water as the waters of Mormon; the verse states that the manner was the same.

title: Authority to Establish Churches
summary: King Mosiah grants Alma authority to establish churches throughout Zarahemla and to ordain priests and teachers, as the people are too numerous for one teacher or one assembly.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah granted Alma authority to establish churches throughout Zarahemla and power to ordain priests and teachers over every church.
There were too many people for one teacher to govern them or for all to hear the word of God in one assembly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah and Alma may be shown together as the grant of authority is reported.
unspecified_visual_details: No formal appointment action or exact setting is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a ceremony or words spoken by Mosiah.

title: The Churches Gather
summary: The people assemble in different bodies called churches, each with priests and teachers. Each priest preaches as Alma delivered the word, and all the churches are one church of God, teaching repentance and faith in God.

explicit_facts.text: The people assembled in different bodies called churches, each with priests and teachers; every priest preached the word as delivered by Alma.
Though many, the churches were one church, the church of God; nothing was preached except repentance and faith in God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Separate assemblies can be represented as distinct groups of church members.
unspecified_visual_details: The buildings, exact number of people in each body, and individual teachers are not specified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The source summarizes the teaching; do not invent sermon dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the churches as a supernatural physical union.

title: Seven Churches in Zarahemla
summary: There are seven churches in Zarahemla. Those who desire to take the name of Christ or God join the churches and are called the people of God; the Lord pours out his Spirit upon them, and they are blessed and prosper in the land.

explicit_facts.text: There were seven churches in the land of Zarahemla, and those desiring to take the name of Christ or God joined them.
They were called the people of God; the Lord poured out his Spirit upon them, and they were blessed and prospered in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The seven churches may be represented by distinct gathered communities.
unspecified_visual_details: The source does not describe the Lord’s Spirit as a visible form or specify a visual sign of blessing and prosperity.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord’s Spirit and the people’s blessing are stated, but no visible appearance or sign is specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure, supernatural light, or other unmentioned manifestation.
